pr_title: lora: Add support for fine-grained STM32WL power amplifier configuration
pr_body:
### Summary

This PR adds the ability to select between the low-power `RFO_LP` and high-power `RFO_HP` LoRa radio power amplifier output, as well as setting the maximum design Tx output via a new devicetree properties on STM32WL-based boards.
This allows better matching of the power amplifier output with boards' RF impedance matching network.

Previously only the high-power `RFO_HP` output was supported in the highest design power output (+22 dBm), as the same PA config register is used to differentiate between the discrete SX1261 and SX1262 chips in LoRaMac-node.

I've locally tested this change on a Olimex STM32WL Devkit.

Closes #48511

### Change Description

Add STM32WL-specific `sx126x_set_tx_params` function based on the STM32CubeWL modifications to LoRaMac-node.

~~Add `tx-power-low` devicetree binding to `st,stm32wl-subghz-radio` for toggling the `RFO_LP` output functionality provided in this commit.~~
**Add the `power-amplifier-output` devicetree property to `st,stm32wl-subghz-radio` for selecting between the RFO_LP and RFO_HP output configurations provided by the above mentioned function.**

Also add the `rfo-lp-max-power` and `rfo-hp-max-power` DT properties for defining the maximum design power of the respective outputs' matching networks.

~~Set `RFO_LP` output as default for the BB-STM32WL module.~~
**Set the appropriate output and max-power values for all affected boards and modules.**
### Impact and future work

I consider this method of least impact for adding this feature and aligning the behavior of the Zephyr LoRa driver for the STM32WL family with that provided by the STM32CubeWL driver. (Versus the alternative of adding the STM32CubeWL LoRaMac-node modifications as its own Zephyr module with accompanying glue code in `sx126x.c`)

This PR may improve `RFO_LP` Tx performance, as it uses the higher duty cycle configured in the STM32CubeWL driver for the +15 dBm output mode. It should also guarantee better device longevity by additionally enforcing overcurrent protection for the power amplifier.

This PR also paves the way for more advanced PA output selection. A `tx-power-gpios` property might later be added for defining GPIOs to control an RF switch to toggle `RFO_LP` and `RFO_HP` on hardware supporting this such as the Nucleo WL55JC.

There are still some differences in hardware configuration to STM32CubeWL that the Zephyr LoRa driver is lacking, such as not setting the highest Rx gain possible in `SX126xSetRxBoosted`, and the LoRaMac-node code assuming a default antenna gain of 2.15 dBi, but I will address these in separate PR(s).

@martinjaeger I'm not sure how you've worked around this issue on your hardware, but if you've re-soldered the 0R resistor to enable the `RFO_HP` output path, you'll need to delete the newly added property in your overlay(s). Just a friendly heads up :smiley:

### References

See chapter RM0461 chapter 4.8.4., Set_PaConfig() command, and AN5457 chapter 5.1.2.

1. [RM0461 Reference manual - STM32WLEx advanced Arm-based 32-bit MCUs with sub-GHz radio solution](https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0461-stm32wlex-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-with-subghz-radio-solution-stmicroelectronics.pdf)
2. [AN5457 Application note - RF matching network design guide for STM32WL Series](https://www.st.com/resource/en/application_note/an5457-rf-matching-network-design-guide-for-stm32wl-series-stmicroelectronics.pdf)
3. [STM32CubeWL SubGHz_PHY driver](https://github.com/STMicroelectronics/STM32CubeWL/blob/main/Middlewares/Third_Party/SubGHz_Phy/stm32_radio_driver/radio_driver.c#L620-L692)
pr_comments: - Amend formatting to comply with coding style guidelines
Direction looks ok to me but I'd like actual and active WL users to provide feedback first
I tested it on custom hardware with STM32WLE5CC and the RFO_LP pin attached. Works fine with the new devicetree flag activated. Thanks! :)

Thanks for the PR. I haven't look at all the details, but overall the approach looks fine to me. I just wonder if the device tree entry shouldn't be an enum with the options "hp" or "lp". Sure it means changing the dts of existing boards, but it's probably less error prone in the long term. It means users really have to select the right output instead of possibly finding that a board doesn't work.

I'll try to review the PR more in details in the next days.

> I just wonder if the device tree entry shouldn't be an enum with the options "hp" or "lp".

I like the idea! I was also thinking about changing the name of this property so it would better describe that it is about selecting `RFO_LP`. We already have following properties for `sx127x`:
- `power-amplifier-output = "rfo";` (which is an enum)
- `rfo-enable-gpios = <&gpios ...>;`

1) so I would add something like:
- `rfo = "hp";`
- `rfo = "lp";`

2) or we could use `power-amplifier-output` just like with `sx127x`:
- `power-amplifier-output = "rfo-hp";`
- `power-amplifier-output = "rfo-lp";`
with following bindings:
```
  power-amplifier-output:
    type: string
    required: true
    description: |
      Selects power amplifier output pin.
    enum:
      - "rfo-lp"
      - "rfo-hp"
```

I think the latter makes more sense and will make it consistent across sx12xx families.

I originally drafted this PR with an enum as well, which would get overridden in `sx126x_set_tx_params` if `DT_INST_NODE_HAS_PROP(0, tx-power-gpios)` evaluated as true.

After some consideration I thought it'd be more likely to be get accepted if it didn't require adding a property to several boards that work with the default `RFO_HP` output exclusively anyway. AFAICT only the BB-STM32WL module doesn't work out of the box without the property selecting `RFO_LP`.

> or we could use power-amplifier-output just like with sx127x:

I do like the idea of matching the structure and behavior of the SX127x driver, so if nobody objects I'll edit the commit to use the original enum property and logic but with the SX127x naming suggested above.

Excluding the GPIO logic though as that's not as cleanly implemented considering how some RF switches are wired.

*See the Nucleo WL55JC schematics, it's not as simple as having a dedicated GPIO line for toggling between `RFO_LP` and `RFO_HP`: the existing `FE_CTRL1` and `FE_CTRL2` lines which are individually used for switching the antenna between Rx and Tx are used for a third state with both lines logic high to toggle the `RFO_LP` output. Adding support for that would require changes to the existing Tx/Rx switch code in `SX126xSetOperatingMode` in the general SX126x driver which I wanted to avoid.
Also there's no guarantee that other boards would implement it similarly with a SP3T switch when the Nucleo is the only currently supported board with a GPIO-togglable LP/HP switch.*

Amended commit to employ enum property suggested above.

The latest commit now specifically adds the `RFO_HP` output selection to the Seeed Studio LoRa-E5 module and Nucleo WL55JC board (here the high-power RF switch output is selected inherently by the driver's behavior in switching the Rx/Tx output GPIOs through `FE_CTRL1` and `FE_CTRL2`. See my previous comment and [here](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/lora/sx126x.c#L287-L288)).

I chose not to define a default `RFO_LP`/`RFO_HP` output in `stm32wl.dtsi`, as this will prompt people with custom/out-of-tree boards to update their devicetree definitions when they run into this, rather than silently enforcing a default which may be incorrect for their use case.

Thanks for the review and your feedback on this @mniestroj @aurel32! :)
Amend commit with C source enum from DT_INST_STRING_UPPER_TOKEN, as suggested by @JordanYates

> Add STM32WL-specific sx126x_set_tx_params function based on the STM32CubeWL modifications to LoRaMac-node.

After reading AN5457, I am a bit concern by that change. Especially the fact that the application notes says "_This is because the RF PA output impedance values change with the RF PA settings._".

The STM32CubeWL does not change the PA config based on the **requested TX power,** but rather on the **maximum design TX power**. I believe that most manufacturers determine the RF matching network based on the maximum TX power allowed by either the LP or HP outputs, so changing the PA config might actually increase the RF mismatch,  reducing the effective TX power.

> The STM32CubeWL does not change the PA config based on the **requested TX power,** but rather on the **maximum design TX power**. I believe that most manufacturers determine the RF matching network based on the maximum TX power allowed by either the LP or HP outputs, so changing the PA config might actually increase the RF mismatch, reducing the effective TX power.

Damn good find, I should've read the application note more thoroughly.

Since we don't set `max_power` anywhere, and the BB-STM32WL module I work with uses the same [matching and filtering network](https://www.olimex.com/Products/IoT/LoRa/BB-STM32WL/resources/BB-STM32WL_RevC.pdf) for both +14 dBm `RFO_LP` and +22 dBm `RFO_HP` outputs (based on the configuration of a 0R resistor), I'd falsely assumed that we could just use the passed `power` value which seems to be based on the max EIRP for the configured region.

I think this calls for adding a DT enum for each output to select the maximum design RF output power of a board, and a rework of the logic that configures the PA based on those values.

On a similar note, I've found another interesting tidbit when traversing the LoRaMac-node code: it assumes 2.15 dBi default antenna gain in all regions, since we don't set the `MIB` antenna gain parameter in the driver. Users with lower gain antennas will find themselves not reaching their region's max EIRP, and users with higher gain ones will possibly be exceeding it (providing high gain antennas are even legal in their regions, EU rules at least seems to stipulate a max gain of 2.15 dBi).

- Add new DT properties `rfo-lp-max-power` and `rfo-hp-max-power`
- Update PA config logic, now functionally matches STM32CubeWL SubGHz driver

I chose to add separate max power properties in order to allow support for boards with runtime configurable low- and high-power outputs sporting independent matching networks (e.g. Nucleo WL55JC). The default values for both are set to match the defaults in the STM32CubeWL driver.

Amended commit with reference to AN5457 in DT binding property description.

Thanks again for the thorough review @aurel32! :smile:
The previous code would've likely set suboptimal PA config values for several board configurations.

Having PA configuration settings to complement matching networks highest Tx output makes perfect sense, now that it's tumbled around my brain for a few hours—seeing how impedance is a function of reactance and resistance, with resistance varying based on power amplifier output current.

Amended commits:

- Add explanation of default value to DT property binding description
- Reword comment explaining `RFO_HP` selection in Nucleo WL55JC board for clarity
- Set `RFO_LP` `max-power` default to +14 dBm
____

> I have tested this PR today and got very nice results :)

Awesome! Thanks so much for testing :heart: 

Appreciate the review and suggestions you two. :)

issue_context.title: STM32WL LoRaWAN pinout incomplete / RFO pin not selectable
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**

The STM32WL chip series has on chip LoRa and provides two input and two output pins for this. The low power output pin (RFO_LP) and the high power output pin (RFO_HP) are currently not choosable. By default the RFO_HP pin is used.

The limitation was found because of the following problem:
A custom board with STM32WLE5CC, which is optimized to only use the RFO_LP pin was configured with two different firmwares.
The first firmware is a bare metal version configured with STM32CubeMX and the second one is the lorawan class a sample from zephyr. The bare metal firmware reached and rssi of around -70 and the zephyr sample only of -110. After connecting the RFO_LP and the RFO_HP pin the zephyr sample reached an rssi of around -60.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
An optimal solution would be an option in the devicetree to select the preferred RFO pin.

**Additional context**
From the Datasheet of STM32WLE5CC
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/108049583/182088170-2f91300e-7610-4f50-b0eb-0cda1abf3f33.png)
comments: Rather looks like a pure LORA driver point.

> An optimal solution would be an option in the device tree to select the preferred RFO pin.

The SX127X driver has such an option, but not the SX126X driver, as both the SX1261 and SX1262 chips only have a single RF output, respectively LP and HP. The HP and LP output seems specific to the ST implementation, and the way to switch is not documented in the STM32WL reference manual, nor in the SX126X manual.

That said it is possible to find the way to switch between the two implementation by looking at STM32Cube. It appears that it uses a modified version of the loramac-node library, and uses the bit that selects between the SX1261 and the SX1262. So you might be able to get the LP output working by changing SX1262 into SX1261 in these lines:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/lora/sx126x_common.h#L25-L27

> Rather looks like a pure LORA driver point.

If that works it should be possible to add a property in the `st,stm32wl-subghz-radio` binding and use it to select the correct chip version.

> The HP and LP output seems specific to the ST implementation, and the way to switch is not documented in the STM32WL reference manual,

IIUC, it's actually documented in §5.8.4:

> Set_PaConfig() command:
byte 3
    bits 7:1 Reserved, must be kept at reset value.
    bit 0 PaSel: PA selection.
      0: HP PA selected
      1: LP PA selected (default)

> IIUC, it's actually documented in §5.8.4:

Indeed I search too quickly through the reference manual. Apologies.

> > IIUC, it's actually documented in §5.8.4:
> 
> Indeed I search too quickly through the reference manual. Apologies.

Took me some time to find it :-D

Thanks, so I am adding this up from you.
According to the STM32WLE5CC RM (https://www.st.com/resource/en/reference_manual/rm0461-stm32wlex-advanced-armbased-32bit-mcus-with-subghz-radio-solution-stmicroelectronics.pdf) in §4.8.4 the Set_PaConfig(PaDutyCycle, HpMax, PaSel, 0x01) sets to LP or HP RFO.

In `modules/lib/loramac-node/src/radio/sx126x/sx126x.c` the function `void SX126xSetTxParams( int8_t power, RadioRampTimes_t rampTime) ` calls the set_PaConfig() function according to the device. This is for SX1261 a LP setting and for SX1262 a HP setting.

> That said it is possible to find the way to switch between the two implementation by looking at STM32Cube. It appears that it uses a modified version of the loramac-node library, and uses the bit that selects between the SX1261 and the SX1262. So you might be able to get the LP output working by changing SX1262 into SX1261 in these lines:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/lora/sx126x_common.h#L25-L27

According to these lines for STM32WL the SX1262 is selected and so HP output is selected. 

So I just changed line 27 from `#define SX126X_DEVICE_ID SX1262` to `#define SX126X_DEVICE_ID SX1261` and it seems to work. My test with the rssi (of course the RFO pins in this case NOT connected) improved from -110 to -70.

An idea for a solution in the zephyrproject discord:

https://discord.com/channels/720317445772017664/883448180950327366/1072593303729623100

Note that until this issue is fixed boards which exclusively use the `RFO_LP` pin can't send LoRa transmissions, and the power amplifier may even be damaged if used in this configuration for longer durations.

I've spent two days debugging until I traced it to the `RFO_` pins configuration and this issue, as my Olimex STM32WL Devkit wasn't sending detectable transmissions.

review_comments: Nice and clever trick, I like it ;-)

Indeed, me too! I didn't think to extract a DT enum string value directly with `DT_STRING_TOKEN`, in retrospect it almost seems obvious.

We can thank @JordanYates for this insight. :)
